definition_zh: 卫生；卫生学；清洁卫生
definition_en: the practice of keeping the body and surroundings clean in order to prevent disease
core_image: 水龙头下搓洗的双手，肥皂泡不断落下
scene: 护士在病房门口提醒实习生先洗手。Before entering the ward, the nurse reminded the intern to practise good hygiene.
sceneCN: 这里 hygiene 是「卫生」（第 1 个义项：为防病而保持清洁的日常做法）；句意：进病房前，护士提醒实习生保持良好卫生。

derivatives.zh: hygiene 加形容词后缀 -ic 构成，义为「卫生的；清洁的」
hygienic 加 -ally 构成，义为「卫生地；清洁地」
hygiene 加表示人的后缀 -ist 构成，义为「卫生师；牙科保健员」

senses.title: Clean habits that protect health
senses.definition: the daily practices, such as handwashing and bathing, that keep the body clean and help prevent disease
senses.definitionCN: 洗手、洗澡等保持身体清洁、帮助预防疾病的日常做法
senses.example: Good hand hygiene is the simplest way to stop infections.
senses.exampleCN: 良好的手部卫生是阻断感染最简单的方法。
senses.why: Greek hygiēs means healthy, and hygieinē technē was the art of health, so the noun first names the habits that serve health.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hygiēs 意为健康的，hygieinē technē 指健康之术，因此这个词最初指为健康服务的习惯。

senses.title: Cleanliness of a place
senses.definition: the condition of a place being clean and free from dirt or germs
senses.definitionCN: 某个场所干净、没有污物或细菌的状态
senses.example: Inspectors checked the hygiene of every kitchen in the hotel.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员检查了酒店每间厨房的卫生状况。
senses.why: Health depends on surroundings as much as on the body, so the same noun shifts from personal habits to the state of a place.
senses.whyCN: 健康既取决于身体，也取决于周围环境，于是同一个词从个人习惯扩展到场所状态。

senses.title: The science of preserving health
senses.definition: the systematic study of the conditions and rules that preserve health
senses.definitionCN: 研究维护健康的条件与规则的系统学科
senses.example: She took a course in hygiene during her nursing training.
senses.exampleCN: 她在护理培训期间修了一门卫生学课程。
senses.why: The Greek phrase meant the art of health as a body of knowledge, and English kept that academic sense alongside the everyday one.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语短语本就把健康之术当作一门知识，英语因此在使用义之外保留了这一学科义。

senses.title: Organized public health measures
senses.definition: collective measures, such as clean water, waste control, and vaccination, that protect a whole community
senses.definitionCN: 清洁供水、废物控制、接种疫苗等保护整个群体的集体措施
senses.example: Public hygiene campaigns cut cholera deaths in the city.
senses.exampleCN: 公共卫生运动降低了这座城市的霍乱死亡人数。
senses.why: When the habits of many people are organized by authorities, personal hygiene becomes a public measure.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人的习惯由当局统一组织时，个人卫生就变成公共措施。

senses.title: Care of the mind
senses.definition: the practice of protecting emotional and mental well-being as if it were a form of cleanliness
senses.definitionCN: 像保持清洁一样保护情绪与心理健康的做法
senses.example: Rest and honest talk are basic mental hygiene.
senses.exampleCN: 休息与坦诚交流是基本的心理卫生。
senses.why: The metaphor of cleanliness extends from the body to the mind, giving a figurative but well-established sense.
senses.whyCN: 「清洁」的比喻从身体延伸到心灵，形成这个比喻化但已固定的义项。

senses.title: Safe handling of food
senses.definition: the handling, storage, and preparation of food in conditions that prevent contamination
senses.definitionCN: 在防止污染的条件下处理、储存和制作食物
senses.example: Food hygiene rules require cooks to wash their hands often.
senses.exampleCN: 食品卫生规则要求厨师经常洗手。
senses.why: Food is one of the routes by which dirt and germs reach the body, so hygiene specializes to the kitchen.
senses.whyCN: 食物是污物与细菌进入身体的通道之一，因此 hygiene 专门用于厨房场景。

senses.title: Protection in the workplace
senses.definition: the control of workplace hazards, such as dust, noise, and chemicals, that can harm workers
senses.definitionCN: 对粉尘、噪声、化学品等可能伤害劳动者的工作场所危害进行控制
senses.example: Occupational hygiene reduced lung disease among miners.
senses.exampleCN: 职业卫生减少了矿工中的肺病。
senses.why: The same protective logic applies to the places where adults spend their working hours.
senses.whyCN: 同样的保护逻辑适用于成年人度过工作时间的场所。

senses.title: Infection control in hospitals
senses.definition: strict cleanliness procedures in medical settings that limit the spread of germs
senses.definitionCN: 医疗机构中限制细菌传播的严格清洁程序
senses.example: Hospital hygiene includes sterilizing instruments and cleaning wards.
senses.exampleCN: 医院卫生包括器械灭菌与病房清洁。
senses.why: Where patients are already weak, the ordinary rules of cleanliness become strict clinical protocol.
senses.whyCN: 在病人本就虚弱的场所，普通的清洁规则会升级为严格的临床规程。

intro.en: Hygiene reaches English through French from the Greek phrase hygieinē technē, the art of health, built on hygiēs, healthy.
intro.cn: hygiene 经法语进入英语，源头是希腊语 hygieinē technē（健康之术），其词干 hygiēs 意为健康的。

items.en: Hygieia, daughter of Asclepius, was worshipped as the goddess of health.
items.cn: 许癸厄亚是阿斯克勒庇俄斯之女，被奉为健康女神。

items.en: The adjective hygiēs describes a healthy, sound body.
items.cn: 形容词 hygiēs 描述健康、健全的身体。

items.en: Hygieinē technē names the art of preserving health.
items.cn: hygieinē technē 指保持健康的技艺。

items.en: Classical Latin used sanitas rather than a borrowed Greek noun for health.
items.cn: 古典拉丁语表达「健康」用 sanitas，而没有借用这个希腊名词。

items.en: French hygiène carries the medical term into the modern languages.
items.cn: 法语 hygiène 把这个医学术语带入现代诸语言。

items.en: English hygiene now covers personal habits, public systems, and specialized fields.
items.cn: 现代英语的 hygiene 已涵盖个人习惯、公共系统与专门领域。

note.en: Hygiene is the noun of health-minded cleanliness, close to its own adjective and to the wider vocabulary of sanitation and asepsis.
note.cn: hygiene 是表示「为健康而清洁」的名词，与自己的形容词以及 sanitation、asepsis 等更广的词汇相邻。

entries.definition: clean and free from disease-causing germs
entries.definitionCN: 卫生的；清洁的

entries.definition: in a way that is clean and safe for health
entries.definitionCN: 卫生地；清洁地

entries.definition: a trained specialist who practises hygiene, especially for teeth
entries.definitionCN: 卫生师；牙科保健员

entries.definition: the state of being clean
entries.definitionCN: 清洁；干净

entries.definition: public systems for removing waste and supplying clean water
entries.definitionCN: 环境卫生；排污设施

entries.definition: the absence of harmful germs, especially in surgery
entries.definitionCN: 无菌；防腐

normalIntro.en: Hygiene is the daily work of health: clean hands, clean food, clean rooms.
normalIntro.cn: hygiene 是每天都做的健康功课：干净的手、干净的食物、干净的房间。

normal.en: Personal hygiene begins with clean hands and a clean body.
normal.cn: 个人卫生从干净的手和干净的身体开始。

normal.en: Food hygiene keeps kitchens and cooks free from germs.
normal.cn: 食品卫生让厨房和厨师远离细菌。

normal.en: Hygiene standards tell staff how clean a place must be.
normal.cn: 卫生标准告诉员工一个场所必须清洁到什么程度。

normal.en: The adjective hygienic describes anything clean and safe for health.
normal.cn: 形容词 hygienic 描述任何清洁且对健康无害的事物。

normal.en: A hygienist is the trained person, while hygiene is the practice.
normal.cn: hygienist 指受过训练的人，而 hygiene 指做法本身。

abstract.en: Picture two hands rubbing soap under a running tap.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在水龙头下搓着肥皂。

abstract.en: Imagine a hospital floor that shines because it was just mopped.
abstract.cn: 想象医院地面刚拖过，亮得反光。

abstract.en: Think of an old medical book that teaches people how to stay well.
abstract.cn: 想象一本教人保持健康的旧医书。

examples.en: Wash your hands often to maintain good hygiene.
examples.cn: 经常洗手以保持良好卫生。

examples.en: The restaurant was closed because its hygiene was poor.
examples.cn: 这家餐馆因卫生状况差而被关停。

examples.en: Better hygiene has cut infection rates in the ward.
examples.cn: 更好的卫生条件降低了病房的感染率。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨，净」——把身上洗得干干净净，才算卫生；这只是谐音联想，并非词源。

root: 希腊语 hygiēs（健康的）→ hygieinē technē（健康之术）→ 法语 hygiène → 英语 hygiene，核心义「为健康而保持清洁」。

sensesIntro.en: Hygiene begins as personal clean habits, widens to the cleanliness of places and organized public measures, then branches into the science of health and into specialized fields such as food, work, the mind, and hospital care.
sensesIntro.cn: hygiene 从个人清洁习惯起步，扩展到场所的清洁与有组织的公共措施，再分出卫生学以及食品、职业、心理、医院护理等专门领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pair of hands under running water, soap bubbles falling.
core.cn: 核心意象：水龙头下搓洗的双手，肥皂泡不断落下。

branches.en: Personal habits form the first and most literal branch.
branches.cn: 个人习惯是最早、最字面的分支。

branches.en: The cleanliness of a place is the state branch.
branches.cn: 场所的清洁是状态分支。

branches.en: The science of health is the academic branch.
branches.cn: 卫生学是学术分支。

branches.en: Organized measures and hospital protocol turn hygiene into public practice.
branches.cn: 有组织的措施与医院规程把卫生变成公共实践。

branches.en: Mind, food, and work are specialized fields that inherit the same protective logic.
branches.cn: 心理、食品与职业是继承同一保护逻辑的专门领域。

intro.en: Hygiene is a Greek medical noun that reached English through French, with hygienic and hygienist built on the same stem.
intro.cn: hygiene 是经法语进入英语的希腊医学名词，hygienic 与 hygienist 都建在同一词干上。

latinIntro.en: Greek hygiēs means healthy, and hygieinē technē means the art of health; Latin expressed the same idea with sanitas.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 hygiēs 意为健康的，hygieinē technē 意为健康之术；拉丁语表达同一概念更常用 sanitas。

items.example: Hygieinē technē takes its first element from hygiēs.
items.exampleCN: hygieinē technē 的第一部分来自 hygiēs。

items.example: Hygieinē technē was the art of health.
items.exampleCN: hygieinē technē 就是健康之术。

items.example: Technē supplies the second half of the Greek phrase.
items.exampleCN: technē 提供这个希腊短语的后半部分。

items.example: Hygieia was honoured as the goddess of health.
items.exampleCN: 许癸厄亚被尊为健康女神。

items.example: French hygiène carried the Greek term into modern languages.
items.exampleCN: 法语 hygiène 把这个希腊术语带入现代语言。

items.example: English hygiene keeps the Greek sense of health.
items.exampleCN: 英语 hygiene 保留了希腊语中「健康」的含义。

items.example: The suffix -ic turns hygiene into hygienic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 把 hygiene 变成 hygienic。

items.example: The suffix -ic forms adjectives such as hygienic.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ic 构成 hygienic 这类形容词。

items.example: The suffix -ist forms the noun hygienist.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ist 构成名词 hygienist。

items.example: A dental hygienist cleans teeth professionally.
items.exampleCN: 牙科保健员专业地清洁牙齿。

definition_zh: 高血压（症）；血压过高；局部循环高压；过度紧张
definition_en: a condition in which blood pressure stays abnormally high, or a state of excessive tension
core_image: 一根被从里面撑紧的血管，压力表指针顶到红区
scene: 中年人体检时两次读数都偏高，医生让他先改善饮食。The nurse explained that his hypertension was mild and could be managed with diet.
sceneCN: 这里 hypertension 是「高血压」（第 1 个义项：血压长期高于正常范围的疾病）；句意为护士说明他的高血压属于轻度，可以通过饮食控制。

collocations.zh: 白大衣高血压（诊室紧张导致的暂时升高）

derivatives.zh: 高血压的；也作名词指高血压患者
抗高血压的；也作名词指降压药
低血压，把 hyper- 换成 hypo- 构成的反义词

senses.title: Persistently high blood pressure
senses.definition: a long-term condition in which the pressure of blood against the artery walls stays above the normal range
senses.definitionCN: 血液对动脉壁的压力长期高于正常范围的慢性病
senses.example: Hypertension often causes no symptoms until the heart or the kidneys are damaged.
senses.exampleCN: 高血压常常没有症状，直到心脏或肾脏受损才被发现。
senses.why: The Greek prefix hyper- means over, and tension is a stretching, so the word pictures an artery stretched tighter than it should be.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语前缀 hyper- 表示「超过」，tension 是「拉紧」，所以这个词描绘的是血管被绷得比应有的更紧。

senses.title: A reading above the line
senses.definition: a blood-pressure measurement that is above the normal range, especially one taken on a single visit
senses.definitionCN: 高于正常范围的血压测量值，尤指单次就诊时的读数
senses.example: Her home monitor showed hypertension on three mornings in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 她的家用血压计连续三个早晨都显示血压偏高。
senses.why: Because the disease is defined by a number, the same word also names the high reading that first reveals it.
senses.whyCN: 因为这种病是靠数值来定义的，所以同一个词也用来指第一次暴露它的那个偏高读数。

senses.title: High pressure in one vessel bed
senses.definition: abnormally high pressure inside one section of the circulation, as in pulmonary or portal hypertension
senses.definitionCN: 某一局部循环内的压力异常升高，如肺动脉高压或门静脉高压
senses.example: Pulmonary hypertension makes the right side of the heart work much harder.
senses.exampleCN: 肺动脉高压使右心室负担加重许多。
senses.why: The core image can be narrowed to a single vessel bed, so clinicians speak of high pressure in the lungs or in the liver.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象可以缩小到某一处血管床，所以临床上会说肺里或肝里的局部高压。

senses.title: Nerves pulled too tight
senses.definition: a state of great or excessive psychological tension in a person or a group
senses.definitionCN: 个人或群体过度紧张、绷得太紧的精神状态
senses.example: Months of waiting left the whole family in a state of hypertension.
senses.exampleCN: 数月的等待让全家人都处在一种过度紧张的状态里。
senses.why: The medical image of a vessel stretched too tight transfers easily to nerves stretched too tight.
senses.whyCN: 血管被绷得过紧的医学意象，很容易转到被绷得过紧的神经上。

senses.title: An overcharged atmosphere
senses.definition: an excessively tense or overwrought quality in a situation, a debate, or a public mood
senses.definitionCN: 局势、争论或公共情绪中过度紧张、一触即发的状态
senses.example: The hypertension of the final week before the vote made quiet compromise impossible.
senses.exampleCN: 投票前最后一周那种高度紧张的气氛，让平静的妥协变得不可能。
senses.why: Once tension becomes a shared mood, any public scene can be described as running at dangerously high pressure.
senses.whyCN: 一旦「紧张」成为一种共同情绪，任何公共场面都可以被形容为在危险的高压下运行。

intro.en: Hypertension joins a Greek prefix to a Latin noun: hyper- means over, and tension comes from tendere, to stretch.
intro.cn: hypertension 把希腊语前缀与拉丁语名词接在一起：hyper- 表示「超过」，tension 出自 tendere「拉紧」。

items.en: Greek hyper meant over, above, or beyond, and it became a productive prefix in scientific English.
items.cn: 希腊语 hyper 意为在上、超过，后来成为科技术语中能产的英语前缀。

items.en: Latin tendere meant to stretch or pull tight, and its noun tensio named a stretching.
items.cn: 拉丁语 tendere 意为拉紧、伸张，其名词 tensio 表示拉伸。

items.en: The noun passed through French into English, where tension first named physical stretching.
items.cn: 这个名词经由法语进入英语，tension 最初指物理上的拉伸。

items.en: English extended tension from a stretched rope to strained nerves and strained relations.
items.cn: 英语把 tension 从绷紧的绳索扩展到紧绷的神经与紧张的关系。

items.en: Hypertension was coined in the 1890s for blood pressure that stays abnormally high.
items.cn: hypertension 在十九世纪九十年代被造出来，指长期异常偏高的血压。

items.en: The cuff and the threshold turned hypertension into a measured diagnosis, split into essential and secondary forms.
items.cn: 血压袖带与诊断阈值使高血压成为可测量的诊断，并区分出原发性和继发性两类。

note.en: Hypotension, tension and hypertensive share the stretching root, while high blood pressure, stress and strain are the everyday neighbours.
note.cn: hypotension、tension 与 hypertensive 共享「拉紧」这个词根；high blood pressure、stress 与 strain 则是日常语义上的邻居。

entries.definition: abnormally low blood pressure
entries.definitionCN: 血压异常偏低，与 hypertension 只差一个前缀。

entries.definition: the state of being stretched tight, or mental strain
entries.definitionCN: 被拉紧的状态，或精神上的紧张；是 hypertension 的后半部分。

entries.definition: relating to high blood pressure, or a person who has it
entries.definitionCN: 与高血压有关的，或指高血压患者。

entries.definition: the everyday name for the same condition
entries.definitionCN: 同一种病的日常说法，比 hypertension 更口语。

entries.definition: pressure or worry caused by a difficult situation
entries.definitionCN: 困境带来的压力或忧虑，对应 hypertension 的引申义。

entries.definition: severe pressure or effort on the body or the mind
entries.definitionCN: 身体或精神承受的沉重压力，与「绷紧」的意象相通。

normalIntro.en: Hypertension is a Latin noun of stretching under a Greek prefix meaning over: pressure pulled past the line.
normalIntro.cn: hypertension 是希腊语「超过」加拉丁语「拉紧」：被拉过界线的压力。

normal.en: Hyper- means over, so hypertension is pressure over the normal line.
normal.cn: hyper- 表示「超过」，所以 hypertension 就是超过正常线的压力。

normal.en: Tension comes from Latin tendere, to stretch.
normal.cn: tension 出自拉丁语 tendere，意为拉紧。

normal.en: The adjective is hypertensive, and a hypertensive is also a person with the condition.
normal.cn: 形容词是 hypertensive，而 a hypertensive 也可以指高血压患者。

normal.en: Antihypertensive drugs push the pressure back down; hypo- is the opposite of hyper-.
normal.cn: antihypertensive 是降压药；hypo- 正是 hyper- 的反义前缀。

normal.en: A reading is written as two numbers, the upper systolic and the lower diastolic.
normal.cn: 血压写成两个数字：上面是收缩压，下面是舒张压。

abstract.en: Picture a rubber tube filled from inside until its wall turns pale and tight.
abstract.cn: 想象一根橡胶管从里面被灌满，管壁发白、绷得紧紧的。

abstract.en: Imagine a gauge needle crossing the red line and staying there.
abstract.cn: 想象压力表的指针越过红线，就停在那里不再回落。

abstract.en: Think of a narrow pipe deep in the lungs taking the full push of the heart.
abstract.cn: 想象肺深处一根细管，独自承受心脏泵出的全部推力。

examples.en: Hypertension is often found during a routine check-up.
examples.cn: 高血压常常在常规体检中被发现。

examples.en: Untreated hypertension can damage the heart, the brain and the kidneys.
examples.cn: 未经治疗的高血压会损害心脏、大脑和肾脏。

examples.en: Pulmonary hypertension is not the same as the common form.
examples.cn: 肺动脉高压与常见的高血压不是一回事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「嗨、怕、疼、身」——血压一高，头就发晕，别嗨、别怕、也别硬撑；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 hyper（在上、超过）＋拉丁语 tendere（拉紧）的名词 tensio（张力）→ 英语 tension → hypertension，字面即「张力过高」，十九世纪末起专指血压长期偏高。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a stretched artery, then names the high reading, a local pressure, and finally any tension pulled too tight.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从被绷紧的血管出发，继而指偏高的读数、局部高压，最后指任何被拉得过紧的紧张状态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an artery stretched tight from the inside, the gauge needle in the red zone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根从里面被撑紧的动脉，压力表指针停在红区。

branches.en: A long-term illness defined by pressure above the normal range.
branches.cn: 一种以压力长期高于正常范围来定义的慢性病。

branches.en: The single high reading that first reveals the illness.
branches.cn: 第一次暴露这个病的那个偏高读数。

branches.en: The same high pressure confined to the lungs or the liver.
branches.cn: 同样的高压被限制在肺部或肝部的循环里。

branches.en: Nerves or a public mood pulled as tight as an overfilled artery.
branches.cn: 神经或公共情绪被绷得像灌满的动脉一样紧。

branches.en: The disease and its number are two views of one measurement.
branches.cn: 疾病与其数值，是同一次测量的两个视角。

intro.en: Hypertension is built from the Greek prefix hyper- and the Latin noun tension, with hypertensive and antihypertensive as its main English relatives.
intro.cn: hypertension 由希腊语前缀 hyper- 与拉丁语名词 tension 构成，主要英语亲属是 hypertensive 与 antihypertensive。

latinIntro.en: Greek hyper means over or beyond; Latin tendere means to stretch, and tensio means a stretching.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语 hyper 意为在上、超过；拉丁语 tendere 意为拉紧，tensio 意为拉伸。

items.example: Tension keeps the Latin sense of stretching.
items.exampleCN: tension 保留了拉丁语「拉伸」的含义。

items.example: Tendere is the source of tension and tense.
items.exampleCN: tendere 是 tension 与 tense 的来源。

items.example: Tensio passed through French as tension.
items.exampleCN: tensio 经由法语成为 tension。
紧绷的肌肉一直处于拉伸状态。

items.meaningCN: 行为或结果的名词后缀

items.exampleCN: 血压正常的；血糖正常的

latinEntries.exampleCN: tendere 生出 tension 与 tense。

latinEntries.example: Tensio is the direct source of tension.
latinEntries.exampleCN: tensio 是 tension 的直接来源。
tensus 描述被拉紧的东西。

definition_zh: 假设；假说；前提；待验证的猜想
definition_en: a proposed explanation or premise that is put forward as a starting point and still has to be tested or proved
core_image: 先在下面垫一块地基，再把论点垒在上面
scene: 实验室的白板上写着一句可以被实验推翻的预测，旁边是涂层样本。 Before the experiment began, the team wrote one sentence on the whiteboard: the new coating should halve the rate of corrosion. That sentence was their hypothesis.
sceneCN: 这里 hypothesis 是「科学假说」（第 1 个义项：提出一个可检验的候选解释）；句意：实验开始前，团队在白板上写下一句话：新涂层应能把腐蚀速度减半。这句话就是他们的假说。

pos.zh: 假设；假说（尤指可检验的科学解释）
前提；被当作论证起点的命题

forms.label: 名词复数（希腊语式，-is 变 -es）

derivatives.zh: 假设的（较少用，与 hypothetical 同义）

senses.title: Scientific hypothesis: a testable explanation
senses.titleCN: 科学假说：可被检验的解释
senses.definition: a proposed explanation for observed facts that can be tested by experiment or further evidence
senses.definitionCN: 针对观察到的事实提出的解释，可通过实验或进一步证据来检验
senses.example: The hypothesis that the coating slows corrosion will be tested on twenty steel plates.
senses.exampleCN: “涂层能减缓腐蚀”这一假说将在二十块钢板上接受检验。
senses.why: A hypothesis is laid under a question the way a foundation is laid under a building: it is put in place first, and the experiment is built on top of it.
senses.whyCN: 假说被垫在一个问题下面，就像地基被垫在房屋下面：它先被放好，实验再在它上面搭建。

senses.title: Logical premise: assumed as a base
senses.titleCN: 逻辑前提：被当作论证底座
senses.definition: a proposition taken as true for the sake of an argument, so that other statements can be built on it
senses.definitionCN: 为了进行论证而被当作真的命题，其他陈述可建立在它之上
senses.example: The proof rests on the hypothesis that every finite set has a largest element.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明建立在“每个有限集都有最大元素”这一前提之上。
senses.why: In logic the word keeps its Greek shape: something is placed underneath the reasoning and left there while the argument stands on it.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑学里，这个词保留了希腊语的形态：某物被放在推理的下方并留在那里，论证则站在它上面。

senses.title: Everyday conjecture: an unproved guess
senses.titleCN: 日常猜想：未经证实的推测
senses.definition: a guess or suggestion offered without enough evidence, in ordinary speech
senses.definitionCN: 日常言谈中在证据不足时提出的猜测或设想
senses.example: My hypothesis is that the keys are still in the car.
senses.exampleCN: 我猜钥匙还在车里。
senses.why: The scientific word has loosened into daily use: any explanation put forward before proof counts as a hypothesis, even when no experiment will follow.
senses.whyCN: 这个科学词已经松动到日常用法里：任何在证实之前提出的解释都算假设，即使后面并不会做实验。

senses.title: Working hypothesis: a temporary guide
senses.titleCN: 工作假设：临时的行动依据
senses.definition: a provisional explanation accepted for the time being because it guides investigation, even if it may later be replaced
senses.definitionCN: 因能指导调查而暂时接受的解释，即使以后可能被替换
senses.example: As a working hypothesis, we assume the leak comes from the north pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 作为工作假设，我们先假定泄漏来自北侧管道。
senses.why: A foundation can be temporary. The working hypothesis is laid down not because it is proved, but because building can start on it today.
senses.whyCN: 地基可以是临时的。工作假设之所以被铺下，不是因为它已被证明，而是因为今天就能在它上面开工。

senses.title: Statistics: the null hypothesis
senses.definition: in statistics, the default proposition that there is no effect or no difference, which a test tries to reject
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中默认“没有效应、没有差异”的命题，检验试图将它推翻
senses.example: The null hypothesis states that the two groups perform equally well.
senses.exampleCN: 原假设称两组表现同样好。
senses.why: Here the word is used backwards: the hypothesis laid underneath the test is the dull one, and the whole apparatus is built to knock it down.
senses.whyCN: 这里的用法是反向的：垫在检验下面的假设是最平淡的那一个，整套装置却是为了把它推倒而搭起来的。

senses.title: Plural hypotheses: rival explanations
senses.titleCN: 复数假说：并排的候选解释
senses.definition: the plural form hypotheses, used when several candidate explanations are held side by side
senses.definitionCN: 复数形式 hypotheses，用于同时持有多个候选解释时
senses.example: The team listed three hypotheses and designed one test to separate them.
senses.exampleCN: 团队列出三个假说，并设计了一项能区分它们的检验。
senses.why: The Greek plural keeps the original -is to -es shift. Once several foundations are laid, the question is which one the evidence will stand on.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语式复数保留了 -is 变 -es 的变化。一旦铺下好几块地基，问题就变成证据会站在哪一块上。

senses.title: Mathematics: a conjecture awaiting proof
senses.definition: in mathematics, a statement believed to be true but not yet proved, such as a named conjecture
senses.definitionCN: 数学中相信为真但尚未证明的陈述，如以人名命名的猜想
senses.example: The Riemann hypothesis has resisted proof for more than a century.
senses.exampleCN: 黎曼猜想已有一个多世纪未能被证明。
senses.why: The mathematical hypothesis is a foundation laid under a whole building that does not yet exist: if it holds, a large structure of proofs can be raised.
senses.whyCN: 数学猜想是垫在一整座尚未存在的建筑下面的地基：只要它成立，一大片证明就能被垒起来。

senses.title: On the hypothesis that: a supposition for argument
senses.titleCN: 以假设为前提：为了推论而假定
senses.definition: in the phrase 'on the hypothesis that', used to grant a supposition temporarily and then reason from it
senses.definitionCN: 在短语 on the hypothesis that 中，暂时承认某一设想并由此推理
senses.example: On the hypothesis that demand stays flat, the new factory would still lose money.
senses.exampleCN: 假定需求保持不变，新工厂仍然会亏损。
senses.why: The phrase marks the foundation being laid on purpose: everyone agrees to stand on it for the length of the argument, and no longer.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语标记的是有意铺下的地基：大家同意在论证期间站上去，论证一结束就不再站了。

senses.title: Original sense: a groundwork
senses.definition: in the earliest English use, a particular statement or groundwork on which other statements rest
senses.definitionCN: 在最早的英语用法中，指承载其他陈述的某一说法或基础
senses.example: The old logic text calls the first principle the hypothesis of the whole argument.
senses.exampleCN: 那本旧逻辑教材把第一原理称为整个论证的基础。
senses.why: Greek hypothesis literally meant 'a placing under', the base or groundwork of a building. The logical sense grew from that physical picture.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 hypothesis 字面意为“放在下面”，即建筑的地基或底座。逻辑义正是从这幅物理画面长出来的。

intro.en: Hypothesis is a Greek word borrowed through French and Latin, and its parts are still visible: hypo- 'under' plus thesis 'a placing'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hypothesis 是经法语和拉丁语借入的希腊词，构词成分至今可见：hypo-“在下”加 thesis“放置”。年代为大致估计。

items.en: First recorded in English meaning 'a particular statement'. The word entered through French hypothese and directly from Late Latin hypothesis.
items.cn: 英语中最早记录于 16 世纪 90 年代，意为“某一具体陈述”。这个词经法语 hypothese 并直接由晚期拉丁语 hypothesis 进入英语。

items.en: The sense 'a proposition assumed and taken for granted, used as a premise' is recorded, the sense that still governs logic and argument.
items.cn: 记录到“被假定并视为当然、用作前提的命题”这一义项，这也是至今支配逻辑与论证的义项。

items.en: Greek hypothesis meant 'base, groundwork, foundation', and in extended use 'basis of an argument, supposition', literally 'a placing under'.
items.cn: 希腊语 hypothesis 意为“底座、地基、基础”，引申为“论证的基础、设想”，字面即“放在下面”。

items.en: The word joins hypo- 'under' and thesis 'a placing, proposition'. Thesis goes back to a reduplicated form of PIE *dhe- 'to set, put', the root also behind do, deed, and theme.
items.cn: 这个词由 hypo-“在下”与 thesis“放置、命题”组合而成。thesis 可追溯到原始印欧语 *dhe-“放置、安放”的重复形式，该词根也是 do、deed、theme 的来源。

items.en: The narrower scientific sense, an explanation to be tested, is recorded. From this point the word belongs to experiment as much as to logic.
items.cn: 较窄的科学义“待检验的解释”有记录。自此这个词既属于逻辑，也属于实验。

items.en: The Greek plural hypotheses is kept unchanged, unlike most English nouns. Hypothetical (1580s) and hypothesize (1738) build the rest of the family; theory and thesis remain distinct neighbours.
items.cn: 希腊语式复数 hypotheses 原样保留，与大多数英语名词不同。hypothetical（16 世纪 80 年代）与 hypothesize（1738）补足了词族；theory 与 thesis 仍是各自独立的邻词。

note.en: The first group separates the plural, the adjective, and the verb built on hypothesis; the second group compares words for explanations and for premises.
note.cn: 第一组把复数、形容词和由 hypothesis 构成的动词分开；第二组比较表示“解释”与“前提”的词。

entries.definition: the plural of hypothesis, not a different word. Greek nouns in -is regularly become -es, so one hypothesis becomes two hypotheses.
entries.definitionCN: hypothesis 的复数，不是另一个词。以 -is 结尾的希腊语名词通常变 -es，所以一个假说变成两个假说。

entries.definition: based on a hypothesis or imagined for the sake of argument. It describes a situation, not a scientific claim, and is often close to 'imaginary'.
entries.definitionCN: 基于假设的，或为论证而设想的。它描述一种情形，而不是一条科学主张，常接近“虚构的”。

entries.definition: to form a hypothesis. The verb names the act of laying the foundation; the noun names the foundation itself.
entries.definitionCN: 提出假说。动词命名“铺地基”的动作，名词命名地基本身。

entries.definition: a coherent set of principles that explains a broad class of facts. A theory is a finished building; a hypothesis is the foundation stone laid before the building is tested.
entries.definitionCN: 解释一大类事实的连贯原理体系。theory 是建成的房屋；hypothesis 是房屋受检前铺下的奠基石。

entries.definition: a proposition put forward and defended in argument, or a long research essay. It shares Greek thesis 'a placing' with hypothesis, but stands on its own rather than under something else.
entries.definitionCN: 在论证中提出并加以辩护的命题，或长篇研究论文。它与 hypothesis 共享希腊语 thesis“放置”，但它是自己站着的，而不是垫在别物之下。

entries.definition: something assumed to be true for the sake of reasoning. It is a near translation of Greek hypothesis and carries less scientific weight.
entries.definitionCN: 为推理而假定为真的事。它几乎是希腊语 hypothesis 的译法，科学分量更轻。

entries.definition: an opinion formed from incomplete evidence. A conjecture is openly a guess; a hypothesis is a guess set up so that it can be tested.
entries.definitionCN: 根据不完整证据形成的看法。conjecture 明说是猜测；hypothesis 则是为了让其可被检验而搭起来的猜测。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and real relatives: hypo- 'under', thesis 'a placing', the Greek plural hypotheses, and the family hypothetical / hypothesize.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与真实同族词：hypo-“在下”、thesis“放置”、希腊语式复数 hypotheses，以及 hypothetical／hypothesize 词族。

normal.en: hypo- means 'under' and thesis means 'a placing'. A hypothesis is something placed under a question so that reasoning can stand on it.
normal.cn: hypo- 表示“在下”，thesis 表示“放置”。hypothesis 就是被放在问题下面、让推理可以站上去的东西。

normal.en: The plural is hypotheses, not hypothesises: Greek -is becomes -es, as in analysis and basis.
normal.cn: 复数是 hypotheses，不是 hypothesises：希腊语式 -is 变 -es，如 analysis、basis 一样。

normal.en: Hypothetical means 'assumed for the sake of argument', and hypothesize means 'to lay that foundation down'.
normal.cn: hypothetical 意为“为论证而假设的”，hypothesize 意为“把这块地基铺下去”。

normal.en: A hypothesis and a thesis share thesis 'a placing', but a thesis stands up to be defended while a hypothesis lies underneath to be tested.
normal.cn: hypothesis 与 thesis 共享 thesis“放置”，但 thesis 立起来供人辩护，hypothesis 则躺在下面等着被检验。

normal.en: The null hypothesis is the dull foundation: it says there is no effect, and the experiment is built to knock it down.
normal.cn: 原假设是最平淡的地基：它宣称没有效应，而实验正是为了把它推倒而搭起来的。

abstract.en: Picture a stone slab laid in soft ground. Nothing is built yet, and the slab may sink or hold, but every later brick depends on it.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石板被铺进软土里。上面还没有建筑，石板可能下沉也可能撑住，但后来的每一块砖都依赖它。

abstract.en: A hypothesis is a bet you can lose: the good ones are laid where a test can reach them, not where they are safe from evidence.
abstract.cn: 假说是一场你可以输掉的赌：好的假说被铺在检验够得着的地方，而不是铺在证据碰不到的安全角落。

abstract.en: When several foundations lie side by side, the experiment is not looking for support but for separation: which slab alone can carry the building?
abstract.cn: 当好几块地基并排铺着，实验要找的不是支撑而是区分：哪一块独自能承起这座建筑？

examples.en: Every experiment begins with a hypothesis, but few survive the first week.
examples.cn: 每个实验都从一个假说开始，但很少有假说能熬过第一周。

examples.en: She treated the rumour as a working hypothesis and went to check the records.
examples.cn: 她把这个传闻当作工作假设，然后去查记录。

examples.en: The two hypotheses predict different results, which is exactly why the test is worth running.
examples.cn: 两个假说预测出不同的结果，这正是这项检验值得做的原因。

dict_mnemonic.text: “嗨，破塞西斯”——嗨，先破开地面、塞一块石板在下面当底座，上面再放待验的想法 → hypothesis 假设、前提

root: 源自希腊语 hypothesis“垫在下面的地基”，由 hypo-“在下”+ thesis“放置”构成，核心是“先垫一块地基，让论点立在上面”。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of hypothesis, all from one gesture: something is placed underneath — a question, an argument, a test, a proof — so that reasoning can stand on it and later be knocked down.
sensesIntro.cn: hypothesis 的九个义项都来自同一个动作：把某物垫在下面——问题、论证、检验、证明——让推理站上去，并在以后被推倒。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a slab laid under a structure that is still to be built and tested.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石板铺在尚待建造、尚待检验的结构之下。

branches.en: TESTABLE CLAIMS: science and mathematics lay a claim underneath and then try to break it with evidence or proof.
branches.cn: 可检验的主张：科学与数学把一条主张垫在下面，再用证据或证明去击打它。

branches.en: FOUNDATION: logic, argumentative supposition, and the oldest sense all keep the literal groundwork.
branches.cn: 地基：逻辑前提、论证中的假定与最古老的义项，都保留了字面上的“垫在下面”。

branches.en: GUESS AND TOOL: daily conjecture has no test attached, while a working hypothesis is laid down so that work can start today.
branches.cn: 猜想与工具：日常猜测后面没有检验，而工作假设被铺下是为了今天就能开工。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the null hypothesis is the plain foundation that the whole test is built to demolish.
branches.cn: 统计学：原假设是最朴素的地基，整套检验却是为了拆掉它而建。

branches.en: RIVALS: several hypotheses stand side by side, and the evidence must choose which slab to stand on.
branches.cn: 竞争者：多个假说并排而立，证据必须选择站上哪一块石板。

intro.en: Hypothesis is a Greek compound borrowed whole: hypo- 'under' plus thesis 'a placing'. English adds -ical, -ly, and -ize, and the same two Greek pieces build a large family.
intro.cn: hypothesis 是整体借入的希腊语复合词：hypo-“在下”加 thesis“放置”。英语加上 -ical、-ly、-ize，同样两个希腊成分还构成一大群词。

latinIntro.en: Late Latin took the Greek word unchanged as hypothesis, and Latin thesis came from the same Greek noun. Medieval Latin suppositio was used to translate hypothesis, which is why supposition still feels like its twin.
latinIntro.cn: 晚期拉丁语原样吸收了希腊词 hypothesis，拉丁语 thesis 也来自同一个希腊名词。中世纪拉丁语用 suppositio 翻译 hypothesis，所以 supposition 至今像是它的双胞胎。

items.meaning: a proposition placed under an argument; a testable explanation
items.meaningCN: 垫在论证下面的命题；可检验的解释（hypo- 在下 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The hypothesis was rejected after the second trial.
items.exampleCN: 第二次试验之后，这个假说被否定了。

items.meaningCN: 两个或更多假说（希腊语式复数 -es）
items.example: Both hypotheses assume the same starting temperature.
items.exampleCN: 两个假说都假定相同的初始温度。

items.meaning: based on a hypothesis; imagined for argument
items.meaningCN: 假设的；为论证而假想的（-ical 构成形容词）
items.example: Consider a hypothetical case in which no one answers.
items.exampleCN: 设想一个无人应答的假想情形。

items.meaning: in an assumed or imagined situation
items.meaningCN: 在假设或假想的情况下（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: Hypothetically, the plan could work if costs fell.
items.exampleCN: 假定成本下降，这个计划理论上可行。

items.meaningCN: 提出假说（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: Researchers hypothesize that the sound guides the fish home.
items.exampleCN: 研究者假设这种声音能引导鱼回到出生地。

items.meaning: under the skin, as an injection
items.meaningCN: 皮下的（如皮下注射；hypo- 在下 + derma 皮肤）
items.example: The nurse prepared a hypodermic needle.
items.exampleCN: 护士准备好了一支皮下注射针。

items.meaning: a body temperature dangerously below normal
items.meaningCN: 低体温；体温过低（hypo- 在下 + therme 热）
items.example: The climbers were treated for hypothermia.
items.exampleCN: 登山者接受了低体温治疗。

items.meaning: a proposition to be defended; a long research essay
items.meaningCN: 待辩护的命题；长篇研究论文（希腊语“放置、命题”）
items.example: Her thesis argues that the two reforms were one process.
items.exampleCN: 她的论文主张这两场改革其实是一个过程。

items.meaning: the direct opposite of a proposition
items.meaningCN: 对立命题；正相反的说法（anti- 反对 + thesis 放置）
items.example: His calm manner is the antithesis of her urgency.
items.exampleCN: 他的从容正是她那种急切的对照。

items.meaning: a putting together of parts into a whole
items.meaningCN: 综合；合成（syn- 一起 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The book is a synthesis of history and economics.
items.exampleCN: 这本书是历史学与经济学的综合。

items.meaning: a phrase placed beside the main sentence; a bracket
items.meaningCN: 插入语；圆括号（para- 旁 + en- 内 + thesis 放置）
items.example: The date appears in parentheses at the end.
items.exampleCN: 日期放在末尾的圆括号里。

latinEntries.meaning: base, groundwork; basis of an argument
latinEntries.meaningCN: 地基、基础；论证的依据（晚期拉丁语原样借入）

latinEntries.structure: Greek thesis, from PIE *dhe- 'to set, put'

latinEntries.meaning: a putting under; assumption, used to translate Greek hypothesis
latinEntries.meaningCN: 放在下面；假定（中世纪拉丁语用来翻译希腊语 hypothesis）

definition_zh: 假设的；假想的；推测的；（逻辑）假言的
definition_en: based on a supposition rather than on established fact, or imagined for the purpose of reasoning
core_image: 一张尚属草稿的建筑图，梁柱用虚线画出，旁边标着问号
scene: 这里指「假设的」。 The engineers tested a hypothetical failure, in which the eastern wall gives way first.
sceneCN: 这里 hypothetical 是「假想的」（第 2 个义项：现实中未发生、为推理而设想）；句意：工程师测试了一种假想的失效情形，即东墙先垮塌。图中可辨识物件：虚线草图、问号标记、测力箭头、模型楼体、计算纸。

pos.zh: 假设的；假想的；推测的；（逻辑）假言的（多作定语，也可作表语）

senses.title: Taken as a premise
senses.titleCN: 作为前提的：先假定、后推理
senses.definition: assumed as a starting point so that consequences can be worked out
senses.definitionCN: 被假定为起点，以便推出后果
senses.example: The proof begins with a hypothetical population of infinite size.
senses.exampleCN: 这个证明从一个假想的无限大总体开始。
senses.why: Greek hypothesis was 'a placing under', a base laid beneath an argument; hypothetical marks what serves as that base.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 hypothesis 意为“放在下面”，即铺在论证之下的基础；hypothetical 标记充当这一基础的事物。

senses.title: Imagined, not observed
senses.titleCN: 假想的：现实中没有发生
senses.definition: existing only in imagination or in a constructed example, not in fact
senses.definitionCN: 仅存在于想象或构造出的例子里，事实中并不存在
senses.example: Consider a hypothetical town of ten thousand people.
senses.exampleCN: 设想一座有一万人的假想城镇。
senses.why: A premise must often be invented to test an idea, and the adjective marks that invented status plainly.
senses.whyCN: 为检验一个想法，前提常须被发明出来，这个形容词便直接标记那种“被发明”的状态。

senses.title: Not yet established
senses.definition: proposed as a possible explanation but not yet confirmed by evidence
senses.definitionCN: 作为可能的解释提出，但尚未获证据确认
senses.example: The link between the two events remains hypothetical.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个事件之间的联系仍属推测。
senses.why: A hypothesis sits below proof: it is supported enough to be worth testing, but not enough to be called fact.
senses.whyCN: 假说位于证明之下：它得到足以值得检验的支持，但还不足以被称为事实。

senses.title: If-then in logic
senses.definition: in logic, describing a conditional statement of the form 'if A then B'
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑中指“如果前一条件成立、则后一结果成立”形式的条件陈述
senses.example: A hypothetical proposition is true unless its antecedent is true and its consequent false.
senses.exampleCN: 假言命题除在“前件真而后件假”时，均为真。
senses.why: Logic names conditionals hypothetical because the second clause is placed under the first, exactly as the Greek word suggests.
senses.whyCN: 逻辑学把条件句称为假言，因为后件被置于前件之下，正合希腊词的字面。

senses.title: A question about an unreal case
senses.titleCN: 假设性提问：法律与调查中的虚拟情形
senses.definition: of a question that asks what would follow in a situation that did not occur
senses.definitionCN: 指询问在未曾发生的情形下会怎样的提问
senses.example: The lawyer put a hypothetical question to the witness about a later departure.
senses.exampleCN: 律师向证人提出了一个关于更晚出发情形的假设性问题。
senses.why: Courts and interviews use invented cases to probe reasoning without asserting facts, which is why the label matters legally.
senses.whyCN: 法庭与访谈用虚构情形探查推理而不主张事实，这正是该标签在法律上重要的原因。

senses.title: Idealized for a model
senses.titleCN: 理论模型的：为建模而理想化
senses.definition: describing an idealized case used in a model, with complicating details deliberately removed
senses.definitionCN: 描述模型中使用的理想化情形，复杂细节被有意去除
senses.example: The hypothetical frictionless surface lets students isolate the force.
senses.exampleCN: 假想的无摩擦表面让学生得以单独考察这股力。
senses.why: Modelling needs clean cases; hypothetical marks the deliberate simplification that makes calculation possible.
senses.whyCN: 建模需要干净的情形；hypothetical 标记的正是使计算可行的有意简化。

senses.title: What might have been
senses.titleCN: 反事实的：与现实相反的设想
senses.definition: describing a counterfactual case in which events went differently from what actually happened
senses.definitionCN: 描述与现实发生情况相反的反事实情形
senses.example: A hypothetical early warning would have emptied the town before the wave.
senses.exampleCN: 一个假想的早期预警本可在浪到之前疏散全镇。
senses.why: Reasoning about causes often requires imagining the same situation minus one factor, and that imagined version is hypothetical.
senses.whyCN: 对因果的推理常需想象去掉某一因素的同一情形，而被想象出的那一版就是假想的。

senses.title: Hedged in tone
senses.titleCN: 试探性的：为缓和语气而虚拟
senses.definition: used to soften a proposal or suggestion by presenting it as merely imagined
senses.definitionCN: 通过把提议说成仅仅是设想来缓和语气
senses.example: Hypothetically, we could move the deadline to June.
senses.exampleCN: 假设一下，我们可以把截止日期挪到六月。
senses.why: Saying a plan is hypothetical lowers its force, inviting discussion without commitment.
senses.whyCN: 把计划说成假设性的，会降低其强制力，从而在不作承诺的情况下邀请讨论。

senses.title: In need of testing
senses.titleCN: 待检验的：可被实验推翻
senses.definition: describing a statement framed so that evidence could in principle refute it
senses.definitionCN: 描述一种在原则上可被证据推翻的陈述
senses.example: A good hypothetical claim tells you what observation would prove it wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 一个好的假设性论断会告诉你什么观察能证明它错了。
senses.why: Science values hypotheses that risk failure; the adjective marks claims open to testing rather than settled truths.
senses.whyCN: 科学重视有失败风险的假说；这个形容词标记的是可受检验的论断，而非已定的真理。

intro.en: Hypothetical comes from Greek hypothetikos, built on hypothesis 'a placing under' from hypo- 'under' and thesis 'a placing'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: hypothetical 出自希腊 hypothetikos，词基为 hypothesis“放在下面”，由 hypo-“在下”与 thesis“放置”构成。年代为约数。

items.en: tithenai meant 'to place, put'. With the prefix hypo- 'under' it produced hypotithenai 'to place underneath, to assume as a basis'.
items.cn: tithenai 意为“放置、摆放”。加前缀 hypo-“在下”，构成 hypotithenai“置于下方、作为基础而假定”。

items.en: hypothesis named a base or a supposition laid under an argument. In Aristotle and later writers it also covered a starting premise in geometry and rhetoric.
items.cn: hypothesis 指铺在论证之下的基础或假定。在亚里士多德及后世作者那里，它也指几何与修辞中的起始前提。

items.en: Latin borrowed hypothesis, and English took it in the 16th century. The plural hypotheses keeps the Greek -es ending.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 hypothesis，英语于 16 世纪引入。复数 hypotheses 保留希腊语 -es 词尾。

items.en: Greek hypothetikos 'fit for a supposition' gave Latin hypotheticus and English hypothetical, recorded from the 16th century.
items.cn: 希腊 hypothetikos“适于作假设的”给出拉丁 hypotheticus 与英语 hypothetical，后者于 16 世纪有记录。

items.en: From the 17th century the word was tied to experimental science, where a hypothesis is a testable proposal rather than a settled truth.
items.cn: 自 17 世纪起，该词与实验科学绑定，其中假说是可检验的提议，而非已定的真理。

items.en: The original technical force of hypothesis in Greek geometry is debated, and the deeper Indo-European root of tithenai is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: hypothesis 在希腊几何中的原始术语含义有争议；tithenai 的更深印欧词根属重构而非有据。

note.en: The first group contains forms from the same hypothesis family; the second contains adjectives about possibility, supposition and fiction.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 hypothesis 词族的词；第二组是关于可能性、假定与虚构的形容词。

entries.definition: The supposition itself. Its plural is hypotheses, not hypothesises; hypothetical is the adjective built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指假设本身；复数是 hypotheses，不是 hypothesises；hypothetical 是由它构成的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb meaning 'by supposition'. It often opens a sentence that softens a proposal.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为“假设地”；常置于句首以缓和提议。

entries.definition: To propose a hypothesis. It names the act; hypothetical describes the status of what is proposed.
entries.definitionCN: 提出假说；命名的是动作，hypothetical 描述所提之物的状态。

entries.definition: A rare shorter form of hypothetical, mostly found in older technical prose.
entries.definitionCN: hypothetical 的罕见短形式，多见过时的技术文本。

entries.definition: Based on theory rather than practice; it can describe a well-established framework, while hypothetical stresses that the case is merely supposed.
entries.definitionCN: 基于理论而非实践；可描述成熟框架，而 hypothetical 强调该情形仅为假定。

entries.definition: Believed to be the case, often with doubt; it records belief rather than a deliberate premise.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为是如此，常含怀疑；记录的是信念，而非有意设定的前提。

entries.definition: Existing only in imagination, with no claim to possible reality; stronger and often dismissive.
entries.definitionCN: 仅存在于想象，并不声称可能为真；语气更强，常含贬义。

entries.definition: Capable of happening; it asserts a real chance, while hypothetical only asks what would follow if.
entries.definitionCN: 有可能发生；断言存在真实机会，而 hypothetical 只问“若如此会怎样”。

entries.definition: Based on conjecture with little evidence; it judges the quality of the guess, which hypothetical does not.
entries.definitionCN: 基于证据稀少的猜测；它在评判猜测的质量，而 hypothetical 不作此评判。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词。

normal.en: hypo- 'under' + thesis 'placing': a supposition placed under an argument.
normal.cn: hypo-“在下”+ thesis“放置”：铺在论证之下的假定。

normal.en: hypothetical scenario, hypothetical question and purely hypothetical are the core frames.
normal.cn: 假想情景、假设性问题、纯属假设是核心框架。

normal.en: The family is hypothesis, hypotheses, hypothesize, hypothetical, hypothetically.
normal.cn: 同族词是 hypothesis、hypotheses、hypothesize、hypothetical、hypothetically。

normal.en: Remember the plural: one hypothesis, two hypotheses.
normal.cn: 记住复数：一个 hypothesis，两个 hypotheses。

normal.en: hypothetical asks 'what if'; theoretical asks 'according to the model'.
normal.cn: hypothetical 问“若如此会怎样”，theoretical 问“按模型如何”。

abstract.en: Picture a foundation stone laid under a building that has not yet been designed.
abstract.cn: 想象一块奠基石被铺在一座尚未设计完的建筑之下。

abstract.en: Picture a sketch drawn in dashed lines, each beam labelled with a question mark.
abstract.cn: 想象一张用虚线画成的草图，每根梁上都标着问号。

abstract.en: Picture two paths splitting at a stone: one taken, one only imagined.
abstract.cn: 想象两条路在一块石头处分岔：一条走过，一条只在想象中。

examples.en: The class worked through a hypothetical epidemic to see how fast a response would be needed.
examples.cn: 课堂上演练了一场假想疫情，以看清需要多快的应对。

examples.en: His explanation is still hypothetical; no experiment has confirmed it.
examples.cn: 他的解释仍属假设，尚无实验证实。

examples.en: In a hypothetical proposition, the 'if' clause supplies the condition.
examples.cn: 在假言命题中，“如果”小句提供条件。

dict_mnemonic.text: “嗨（hy）破（po）题（thetical）”——先假设一个题目再想答案 → hypothetical 假设的、假想的

root: 希腊 hypothesis“置于下方”← hypo-“在下”+ thesis“放置”（tithenai“放”）；希腊 hypothetikos → 拉丁 hypotheticus → 英语 -al。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses all rest on one gesture: a premise is laid under a question so that consequences can be followed. Logic, law, modelling and polite hedging each use that gesture.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项都立足于同一个动作：把一个前提铺在问题之下，以便顺出后果。逻辑、法律、建模与礼貌的缓和都使用这一动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a foundation stone under a building that exists only as a dashed sketch.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块奠基石，托着一座只用虚线画出的建筑。

branches.en: THE BASE: a premise under an argument and an idealization inside a model are both stones laid first.

definition_zh: 识别；身份的确认；身份证件；认同；（生物学）物种鉴定
definition_en: the act of recognizing something or establishing who someone is, the document that proves identity, or a feeling of belonging with another person or group
core_image: 把一样陌生的东西放到已知的格子里，两者严丝合缝地对上
scene: 这里指「识别」。 The botanist spent the morning on the identification of a moss she had never seen before.

senses.title: Recognizing something as known
senses.definition: the act of recognizing something and placing it in a known category
senses.definitionCN: 认出某物并把它归入已知类别的行为
senses.example: The identification of the unknown mineral took two days.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴定这种未知矿物花了两天。
senses.why: Idem means 'same' and facere means 'make'. To identify is literally to make one thing the same as a known thing, and the noun names that matching act.
senses.whyCN: idem 意为“相同”，facere 意为“使”。identify 字面上就是使一物与已知之物相同，这个名词命名的正是那次配对动作。

senses.title: Establishing who a person is
senses.definition: the process of determining the name or identity of a person
senses.definitionCN: 确定某人姓名或身份的过程
senses.example: Identification of the passenger was delayed for hours.
senses.exampleCN: 确认这名乘客的身份被耽搁了数小时。
senses.why: The same matching act now runs between a face and a record. The word keeps the legal and administrative tone of a file being checked.
senses.whyCN: 同一个配对动作现在发生在面孔与档案之间。这个词保留了核对档案时的法律与行政语气。

senses.title: A document proving who you are
senses.definition: an official document such as a card or passport that proves a person's identity
senses.definitionCN: 身份证、护照等证明个人身份的官方文件
senses.example: You need two forms of identification to enter the building.
senses.exampleCN: 进入这栋楼需要出示两份身份证件。
senses.why: The abstract act is compressed into a paper object: the card stands in for the matching so that a stranger can check it quickly.
senses.whyCN: 抽象的配对行为被压缩成一张纸：卡片代替了核对过程，让陌生人也能快速查验。

senses.title: Feeling at one with someone
senses.definition: a feeling of closeness in which one shares another person's situation or group's character
senses.definitionCN: 分享他人处境或群体特质、感到亲近的情感
senses.example: Her identification with the villagers grew during the drought.
senses.exampleCN: 在干旱期间，她对村民的认同感增强了。
senses.why: Here the 'same-making' happens inside the self: the boundary between you and another group is treated as if it could be removed.
senses.whyCN: 这里的“使相同”发生在自我内部：你与另一个群体之间的边界被当作可以撤除。

senses.title: Matching a specimen to a species
senses.definition: in biology, the determination of the species to which a specimen belongs
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中确定标本所属物种的工作
senses.example: Correct identification of the beetle depended on the shape of its antennae.
senses.exampleCN: 正确鉴定这种甲虫取决于其触角形状。
senses.why: Taxonomy is matching at its purest: the specimen must be made the same as a named type, and the noun records that forensic sorting.
senses.whyCN: 分类学是最纯粹的配对：标本必须与命名模式相同，这个名词记录的就是这种辨类工作。

senses.title: Treating two things as one
senses.titleCN: 逻辑与数学中的视为等同
senses.definition: in logic and mathematics, the act of treating two distinct expressions or objects as the same
senses.definitionCN: 逻辑与数学中把两个不同表达式或对象当作同一的做法
senses.example: Identification of the two variables shortened the proof.
senses.exampleCN: 把两个变量视为等同，使证明变短了。
senses.why: The original sense 'make same' is used technically: two symbols are declared to stand for one object, and the proof proceeds as if there were no gap.
senses.whyCN: 原义“使相同”被技术化使用：两个符号被宣布代表同一个对象，证明便当作不存在间隙那样推进。

senses.title: A mark that identifies
senses.definition: a label, colour code or mark attached to something so that it can be recognized
senses.definitionCN: 附着于某物、使其可被识别的标签、色码或标记
senses.example: Each blood sample has a colour-coded identification.
senses.exampleCN: 每份血样都有彩色编码的识别标识。
senses.why: The abstract act becomes a visible object again. The mark carries the matching information so that the match can be repeated by anyone.
senses.whyCN: 抽象行为再次变成可见的东西。标识承载配对信息，使任何人都能重复这次配对。

senses.title: Taking on another's role in the mind
senses.definition: in psychology, the unconscious adoption of another person's characteristics or role
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中无意识地吸收他人特质或角色的过程
senses.example: Identification with the hero lets the reader feel his fear.
senses.exampleCN: 对主人公的认同让读者感受到他的恐惧。
senses.why: Psychoanalysis borrowed the everyday sense and made it unconscious: the self quietly makes itself the same as a model, without announcing the copy.
senses.whyCN: 精神分析借用了日常义并使之无意识化：自我悄悄把自己变得与某个榜样相同，却不宣布这次模仿。

intro.en: Identification is a Medieval Latin verb wearing a French noun suffix: idem 'same' plus facere 'make' produced identificare, and French turned it into identification. Every sense still performs the same little operation, making one thing equal to another.
intro.cn: identification 是拉丁动词披着法语名词后缀：idem“相同”加 facere“使”构成 identificare，法语再把它变成 identification。每个义项都仍在做同一个小动作——使一物等于另一物。

items.en: The root behind facere, 'to make or put', is reconstructed as *dhe- and is generally believed to underlie Latin facere, Greek tithenai and English do.
items.cn: facere“做、放置”背后的词根被重构为 *dhe-，一般认为是拉丁语 facere、希腊语 tithenai 与英语 do 的共同来源。

items.en: Idem, 'the same', joined facere, 'to make', in the Medieval Latin verb identificare, 'to make the same'. The compound is late and technical, not classical.
items.cn: idem“相同”与 facere“使”在中古拉丁动词 identificare“使相同”中结合。这个复合词出现较晚，属技术用语，并非古典拉丁造词。

items.en: The suffix -ficare built verbs meaning 'to make', as in aedificare and modificare. Its noun partner -ficatio produced abstract nouns of making.
items.cn: 后缀 -ficare 构成意为“使……”的动词，如 aedificare、modificare；其名词伙伴 -ficatio 造出表示“使之”的抽象名词。

items.en: French formed identification as an administrative and philosophical term. English adopted it in the 17th century, first for the act of treating things as the same.
items.cn: 法语把 identification 造成行政与哲学术语。英语在 17 世纪借入，最初指“把事物视为同一”的行为。

items.en: Police records and taxonomic botany gave the word its everyday and scientific senses: identifying a suspect, identifying a specimen. The document sense follows from police practice.
items.cn: 警务档案与植物分类学赋予这个词日常义与科学义：确认嫌疑人、鉴定标本。证件义则从警务实践中派生。

items.en: Psychoanalysis added the inward sense, identification with a person or group. The word now names both an external check and an internal bond.
items.cn: 精神分析补充了向内的义项：对某人或某群体的认同。这个词现在同时命名外部核对与内部联结。

note.en: The look-alike group separates the verb, the two nouns and the adjective built on idem. The meaning group compares words for checking, recognizing and belonging.
note.cn: 形近组区分同一 idem 词基上的动词、两个名词与形容词；词义组比较表示核对、认出与归属的词。

entries.definition: to recognize, to establish who someone is, or to treat two things as the same. It is the action behind every sense of the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 认出、确认身份或把两物视为相同。它是名词各义项背后的动作。

entries.definition: who or what a person or thing is, or the sameness of two things. It names the result, not the checking process.
entries.definitionCN: 人或物是谁、是什么，或两物之间的一致。它命名结果，而非核对过程。

entries.definition: exactly the same. It states the equality that identification tries to establish, without any act of checking.
entries.definitionCN: 完全相同的。它陈述 identification 试图建立的相等，却不含核对动作。

entries.definition: the act of knowing that something seen or heard before is familiar. It starts from memory, while identification starts from a record or a category.
entries.definitionCN: 认出见过或听过之物为熟悉的。它从记忆出发，而 identification 从档案或类别出发。

entries.definition: the act of proving that a claim or document is true. It tests accuracy, while identification establishes who or what something is.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某个说法或文件为真的行为。它检验准确性，而 identification 确定其身份或类别。

entries.definition: the process of proving that something is genuine, especially a signature or a digital user. It certifies origin rather than category.
entries.definitionCN: 证明某物为真品的过程，尤指签名或数字用户。它认证来源，而非归类。

entries.definition: the state of being officially connected with an organization. It is close to sense 04 but names membership, not felt closeness.
entries.definitionCN: 与某组织正式联系的状态。它接近第 4 义项，但指成员身份，而非情感上的亲近。

normalIntro.en: These hooks build the word from idem 'same' plus facere 'make', then let the matching image cover documents, species and groups.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩从 idem“相同”加 facere“使”搭起这个词，再用配对意象覆盖证件、物种与群体。

normal.en: Split it as idem + facere: make the same. Identification is same-making turned into a noun.
normal.cn: 拆成 idem 加 facere：使相同。identification 就是“使相同”变成名词。

normal.en: Picture a passport photo being laid over a face: the two shapes must line up exactly.
normal.cn: 想象把护照照片盖到一张脸上：两个轮廓必须严丝合缝地重合。

normal.en: In biology the same lining-up happens between a specimen and a named type.
normal.cn: 生物学中同一种重合发生在标本与命名模式之间。

normal.en: When you feel identification with a group, you quietly lay your own shape over theirs.
normal.cn: 当你对某个群体产生认同时，你是悄悄把自己的轮廓盖到他们的轮廓上。

normal.en: Remember the chain: identify the thing, then show identification, then feel identification.
normal.cn: 记住这条链：先 identify 认出来，再出示 identification 证件，最后产生 identification 认同。

abstract.en: Keep one operation in mind: two things are placed on top of each other until the seam disappears.
abstract.cn: 只记一个动作：两样东西被叠在一起，直到接缝消失。

abstract.en: Treat the word as the formal name for 'this is that': every sense says an unknown equals a known.
abstract.cn: 把这个词当作“此即彼”的正式名称：每个义项都在说未知等于已知。

abstract.en: Notice that even the feeling of belonging is described as a matching, not as a gift.
abstract.cn: 注意连归属感也被描述成一次配对，而不是一份礼物。

examples.en: Accurate identification of the disease depends on early testing.
examples.cn: 准确识别这种疾病取决于早期检测。

examples.en: Please bring photo identification to the interview.
examples.cn: 面试时请携带带照片的身份证件。

examples.en: The children's identification with their new school grew quickly.
examples.cn: 孩子们对新学校的认同感很快增强了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音“挨得替非可伸”：窗口前挨个递上证件，工作人员伸手核对，才能确认身份。

root: 中古拉丁 identificare“使相同”（idem 相同 + facere 使），名词形式 identificatio 经法语 identification 进入英语；核心是“把未知之物对到已知之物”。

sensesIntro.en: One Latin phrase, 'make the same', runs through all eight senses. A mineral is matched to a category, a face to a record, a card to a person, a reader to a hero, a beetle to a species, a symbol to another symbol, a mark to an object. Identification is always a joining operation, never a discovery from nothing.
sensesIntro.cn: 一句拉丁语“使相同”贯穿八个义项：矿物对到类别，面孔对到档案，证件对到本人，读者对到主人公，甲虫对到物种，符号对到符号，标识对到物件。identification 始终是一次接合动作，而不是凭空发现。

core.en: Making one thing equal to another so that the pair can be treated as one.
core.cn: 使一物等于另一物，从而可以把这一对当作一体。

branches.en: CHECKING: a thing or a person is matched to a known record.
branches.cn: 核对：某物或某人被对到已知档案。

branches.en: OBJECTS: the match is carried by a card or a mark.
branches.cn: 物件：配对由证件或标识承载。

branches.en: INWARD: the self makes itself the same as a person or group.
branches.cn: 向内：自我把自己变得与某人或某群体相同。

branches.en: SCIENCE: a specimen is matched to a named species.
branches.cn: 科学：标本被对到命名物种。

branches.en: LOGIC: two expressions are declared to stand for one object.
branches.cn: 逻辑：两个表达式被宣布代表同一个对象。

intro.en: Identification stacks idem, the verb-forming -ficare and the noun suffix -atio. The items below show the same base with other endings and show what happens when the 'same' is claimed too strongly.
intro.cn: identification 叠了 idem、动词后缀 -ficare 与名词后缀 -atio。下列条目展示同一词基配其他词尾，并展示“相同”被说得过头时的结果。

latinIntro.en: The Latin entries give the pronoun and the verb behind the compound. They explain why a word about identity also yields words about being identical.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语条目给出复合词背后的代词与动词。它们解释了为什么一个关于身份的词同时产生“完全相同”的词族。

items.meaning: the act of recognizing or proving identity
items.meaningCN: 识别或证明身份的行为
items.example: Identification of the remains took weeks.
items.exampleCN: 遗骸的身份确认花了数周。

items.meaning: to recognize; to establish; to treat as the same
items.example: Can you identify the author of this note?
items.exampleCN: 你能认出这张便条的作者吗？

items.meaning: who or what someone is; sameness
items.example: The thief hid his identity for years.
items.exampleCN: 那个窃贼隐藏身份多年。
这对双胞胎穿着完全相同的外套。

items.meaning: a symbol or mark that names an item
items.meaningCN: 命名某项事物的符号或标记
items.example: Each record has a unique identifier.
items.exampleCN: 每条记录都有唯一标识符。
那件东西几乎无法辨认。

items.example: An unidentifiable smell filled the room.
items.exampleCN: 一股无法辨认的气味充满了房间。

items.example: Both machines were identically set up.
items.exampleCN: 两台机器以完全相同的方式设置。

definition_zh: 认出；识别；确定
definition_en: to recognize someone or something, or to find out exactly what it is

scene: 证人从一排人中认出了嫌疑人。The witness identified the suspect in the lineup.
sceneCN: 这里 identify 是「认出」（第 1 个义项）；句意：证人从一排人中认出了嫌疑人。

senses.title: To recognize
senses.definition: to recognize someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 认出某人或某物
senses.example: The witness identified the suspect in the lineup.
senses.exampleCN: 证人从一排人中认出了嫌疑人。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of recognition.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常的辨认义项。

senses.title: To determine
senses.definition: to find out exactly what something is
senses.definitionCN: 查明某物究竟是什么
senses.example: Scientists identified the cause of the illness.
senses.exampleCN: 科学家确定了这种疾病的原因。
senses.why: Here the mind names the cause, not a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里确定的是原因而非人。

senses.title: To associate oneself
senses.definition: to feel that one shares the feelings of someone
senses.definitionCN: 感到与某人有共同感受
senses.example: She identifies with the young heroine.
senses.exampleCN: 她认同那位年轻的女主人公。
senses.why: The word turns inward toward sympathy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词转向内心的共鸣。
